summary: Octagonal wooden lighthouse at the north end of Grand Manan, first lit in 1860; still an active aid, with a keepers' society and tours of the tower.

lens.note: LighthouseFriends dates the fourth-order lens and occulting signal to 1907; the Department's report for the year ended 30 June 1909 records the change from fixed white to occulting white

structures.type: octagonal wooden tower, shingled, lantern on top
structures.note: Contract 1859; lit 7 July 1860; Rowlett gives 16 m (53 ft) tower

access.note: Village-owned; the Swallowtail Keepers Society manages the site; tower tours and museum open in summer

visit.tours: Keepers Society tours; admission $2 per person

facts.agency: Village of Grand Manan (owner); Swallowtail Keepers Society (site manager)

events.note: Contract let to John P. McKay of Saint John; lantern room finished the next spring
First lit 7 July 1860 by Keeper Jonathan Kent
Bridge built from the point to the headland
Saxby Gale (4 October 1869): station boat destroyed, landing slip washed away, foundation damaged; stone wall built under the tower
Reflectors replaced by a lens (catoptric to dioptric)
Fourth-order French lens and Chance vapour installation (LighthouseFriends date; the Department records the light change in its 1909 report)
Fourth-order fixed white light changed to occulting white, visible 4 seconds, eclipsed 2 seconds (Department report, year ended 30 June 1909)
Wooden building to house a fog bell completed for $974 (G. N. Breen); moved beside the tower in 1920
August 1936: keeper's wife overfilled the burner and her clothes caught fire; flames put out in the lantern room; she died the next day
New keeper's dwelling built; the old one torn down
Last resident keeper left in 1986 when the light was automated
Property transferred to the Village of North Head (LighthouseFriends)
Property transferred to the Village of Grand Manan (LighthouseFriends); Rowlett gives 2012 for the transfer to the village
Twenty-year lease from the village to the Swallowtail Keepers Society signed 2 November 2009
Lantern room replaced by Coast Guard helicopter lift on 10 June 2019; new aluminum lantern with a fourth-order Fresnel lens lit by LED

notes_for_editor: 1) OWNERSHIP CONFLICT, unresolved. The Lighthouse Directory gives transfer to the Village of Grand Manan in 2012. LighthouseFriends gives the Village of North Head in 1994, then the Village of Grand Manan in 1996. The story gives both. 2) SHIPWRECK DATE AND COUNT, unresolved. The New-York Tribune (27 January 1857, p. 3, Eastport dispatch of 26 January) gives 'the 10th inst.' and says eight men of twenty-nine were saved. LighthouseFriends gives 19 January 1857 at 1 a.m. and seven other crew saved. The story states both. 3) FOCAL PLANE of the 1860 light: LighthouseFriends gives 148 ft (about 45 m); the Coast Guard list gives 37.1 m (122 ft) for the present light. The story uses only the Coast Guard figure. 4) LENS AND LIGHT-CHANGE YEAR: LighthouseFriends dates the fourth-order lens and the occulting signal to 1907. The Department's report for the year ended 30 June 1909 (archive.org 1910v44i11p21_0659, printed p. 72, scan p. 79) records the change from fixed white to occulting white. Both are in the story. 5) KEEPER NAME AND DATE, OCR-matched: the Department's 1905 keepers' table (archive.org 1906v40i9p21_0345, scan p. 341, printed p. 260) reads 'Dalzell, Geo. Y | Swallow Tail | Mar. 18, 1893' on one OCR line. The 1907 table (scan p. 149) reads 'Dalzell, Geo. Y Swallow Tail Mar.'. The image was opened in the browser but was not legible enough to confirm the row. Name, station and date were matched by position on the OCR line, so the page image should be checked. The story prints the table's own form 'Dalzell, Geo. Y' and notes LighthouseFriends' 'George T.'. 6) NOT USED: G. A. Lahey 'Oct. 29, 1912' in the Department's 1915 keepers' table (scan p. 75) could not be matched to Swallow Tail with confidence. 7) WALTER GRIFFIN and ADDISON NAVES: LighthouseFriends lists the names with no years. Added to the roster with null years and no role beyond 'keeper'. 8) FOG SIGNAL: the Lighthouse Directory gives a fog horn; LighthouseFriends describes a fog bell house (1914). The Coast Guard list gives a fog horn. The story says only the fog bell house. 9) CHARACTERISTIC: Wikidata's 'Fl4 s; eclipse 2s' is not the Coast Guard's 'Oc W 6s' (flash 4 s, eclipse 2 s); the Coast Guard value is used. 10) ACCESS AND OPENING: the Lighthouse Directory says the tower is open daily in summer; LighthouseFriends says tower opened for occasional tours; the Keepers Society and AHNB say visitors can climb 54 steps and admission is $2. Not checked by phone or visit; the story tells visitors to check before going. 11) PRIVACY: Grimmer A. Ingersoll is named in his public role only (keeper, 1960 to 1986). The keeper's daughter quoted by LighthouseFriends and the 1936 son are not named. 12) The 1859 contract sum is omitted (currency garbled in the cached copy). 13) COPYRIGHT: LighthouseFriends is a copyrighted site. In the fact-check, its wording was paraphrased; the only direct quotations left are from public-domain government reports, the register and the Coast Guard list, and the 1857 newspaper. The Keepers Society's tour page is paraphrased. 14) The brief gives the local unit as Charlotte County; no source read names the county, so the story does not name it.
